items.title: Trials used capsule extracts
items.body:
Shilajit's human trials did not test gummies. They used purified, standardized extracts in capsules, as in a 2019 strength trial and a 2022 bone trial.

A gummy is a different format. That is fine, but it means the label, not the research, tells you what you get.
items.evidence: Study design of the cited RCTs
items.alt: Raw mineral rock, a dish of dark resin and a dish of dark gummies on travertine

items.title: Testosterone rose in older men
items.body:
In a 90-day placebo-controlled trial, healthy men aged 45 to 55 took purified shilajit twice daily.

Total and free testosterone rose significantly versus placebo. Men only, one extract, one trial: a signal worth knowing, not a promise.

chart.title: Purified shilajit vs placebo
chart.source: Pandit S et al. Andrologia 2016;48(5):570-575. Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 250 mg purified shilajit twice daily.

items.evidence_label: Human RCT · Pandit et al., Andrologia 2016

items.title: Read the extract line
items.body:
Gummy labels can list shilajit two ways: the extract itself, or a larger raw-resin equivalent based on a ratio such as 10:1.

The trials report extract amounts. So when you compare products, or compare a label with a study, compare extract with extract.
items.evidence: Label reading; extract amounts per Pandit 2016, Keller 2019, Pingali 2022
items.alt: A magnifying glass on a blank card beside dark gummies on travertine
items.evidence_label: Label literacy · how trials report amounts

items.title: Strength held up at a higher dose
items.body:
In an 8-week trial, 63 active men took a lower dose, a higher dose or placebo, then did a hard leg-fatigue test.

Among the stronger half, the higher-dose group lost 8.9% of strength versus 16.0% on placebo. The lower dose matched placebo.
items.evidence: Human RCT, J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2019

chart.title: Strength lost after fatigue (lower is better)
chart.source: Keller et al., JISSN 2019. 63 men, 8 weeks, 500 vs 250 mg/day PrimaVie shilajit vs placebo; adjusted mean % decline in MVIC, upper-50th-percentile strength subgroup.

items.evidence_label: Human RCT · Keller et al., JISSN 2019

items.title: Blends: check each herb's amount
items.body:
Many shilajit gummies add herbs like ashwagandha. Those herbs have their own trials, at their own doses.

In one 60-day trial, ashwagandha root extract lowered stress scores and cortisol versus placebo. Compare a blend's amounts with the doses used in trials like that.
items.evidence: Human RCT (ashwagandha only), Indian J Psychol Med 2012
items.alt: Dried ashwagandha roots, a bowl of root powder and fresh ginger on linen
items.evidence_label: Human RCT (ashwagandha only) · Chandrasekhar et al., 2012

items.title: No trial tested shilajit gummies
items.body:
We found no published trial of shilajit in gummy form, or of shilajit blended with these herbs.

So a gummy's case rests on the separate ingredient research plus convenience. Many people simply find a pre-measured gummy easier than a sticky resin.
items.evidence: Evidence gap: Europe PMC search 2026-10-08, no shilajit gummy or blend trial to cite
items.alt: Printed research papers, reading glasses and a dish of dark gummies on linen
items.evidence_label: Literature check · no gummy or blend trial found

items.title: Ask about batch lab testing
items.body:
Ayurvedic products can carry heavy metals. A JAMA study found lead, mercury or arsenic in 20.7% of Ayurvedic products bought online.

Before buying any shilajit product, ask the seller whether a lab report exists for your batch.
items.alt: Laboratory glassware and a blank clipboard on a travertine bench
items.evidence_label: Product testing · Saper et al., JAMA 2008

bridge.title: If a gummy fits your routine
bridge.body:
The trials tested daily use for weeks or months. A pre-measured gummy takes the guesswork out of each serving.

One option: Premium Himalayan Shilajit Gummies pair shilajit extract with ashwagandha, gokshura, black musli and four more botanicals. Its pack lists 75% Fulvic Acid and 85+ Trace Minerals; its extract per serving is lower than in the trials above.

Taking medication? Check with your doctor first.
